[BURSEVI:v8p244/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Abundant provision usually increases transgression, though a poor person can also be arrogant and unjust; poverty more often humbles, while wealth more often provokes rebellion, so universal abundance would make corruption prevail.

[ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report says that when God loves a servant, He protects him from worldly life as one protects a sick person from water.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | God owns the heavens and earth, whose realms submit to Him; as creator of beings, He chooses messengers and may legislate for this community as for earlier ones.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The polytheists have no proof beyond imitating leaders of disbelief who instituted idolatry and planted doubts among them.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The surah warns of Judgment and the approaching Hour, describing idolaters' punishment while alluding to believers' honor.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Reflection shows that the Prophet does not invent claims about God, since God would not allow him to attribute words falsely to Him.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | If everyone were affluent, the social order would collapse: some wealthy people would oppress others, victims would resist, and the cycle would produce widespread disorder.

[TABATABAI:42:27#2/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The baseline divine practice is to measure provision with regard to what will set people’s condition right; their welfare affects the amount allotted.

[TABATABAI:42:27/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The following verses also contain summaries of rulings, warnings, admonition, calls to truth, and many points of doctrine.
